q: What drives emissions at an EDC and vinyl chloride plant?
title: EDC and vinyl chloride plant emissions
short: Ethylene and chlorine make EDC, which is cracked in fired furnaces to vinyl chloride. Furnace fuel is the largest direct source, with vent gas incineration and oxychlorination off-gas adding CO2. Chlorine's electricity sits upstream in Scope 3 unless made on site.
audience: PVC producers and buyers of PVC resin

ul: Fuel for the EDC cracking furnaces.
Vent gas and liquid waste incinerators.
Chlorine, from electrolysis, bought in or made in a chlor-alkali unit on site.

p: IPCC 2006 Volume 3 covers EDC and vinyl chloride under petrochemicals. If chlorine is made on site, its electricity becomes your Scope 2 and should be shown as its own line.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
